Thin chocolate chip cookies are your ticket to that perfect mix of whisper thin crunch and melty chocolate pockets, the kind that reminds you of sunny kitchen days and cozy afternoon treats. Butter and brown sugar cream together with a hint of vanilla and a spoonful of Greek yogurt for delicate texture, while mini chips scatter through every bite. A light sprinkle of sea salt lifts the sweetness and keeps these thin chocolate chip cookies irresistibly snackable, whether you dunk them in a cold glass of almond milk or enjoy them warm straight from the tray.

Why You’ll Love This pho meatballs

  • Easy to make, perfect for weeknight dinners.
  • Customizable with your favorite veggies and noodles.

pho meatballs

Discover the ultimate pho meatballs recipe! Enjoy flavorful homemade meatballs in a savory broth that will warm your soul. 🍜✨
Print Recipe Pin Recipe
Prep Time 15 minutes mins
Cook Time 20 minutes mins
Total Time 35 minutes mins
Servings: 6 servings
Course: Main Course
Cuisine: Vietnamese
Calories: 350
Ingredients Equipment Method Notes

Ingredients
  

Meatball Ingredients
  • 1 lb ground beef Main protein for the meatballs.
  • 1/2 lb ground chicken Substitute for pork, adding lean flavor.
  • 1 small onion Minced for depth of flavor.
  • 2 cloves garlic Minced for an aromatic kick.
  • 2 tbsp fish sauce Brings umami to the meatballs.
  • 1 tsp salt Enhances overall taste.
  • 1/2 tsp black pepper A touch of heat.
  • 1 tsp sugar Balances the flavors.
  • 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon Adds warmth.
  • 2 pieces star anise Infuses traditional pho flavor.
Broth and Garnishes
  • 6 cups beef broth The savory base for the soup.
  • to taste rice noodles For a filling component.
  • to taste fresh basil Garnishing for freshness.
  • to taste cilantro Adds a burst of flavor.
  • to taste lime wedges To brighten the dish.
  • to taste bean sprouts For crunch.
  • to taste sliced chili For a spicy kick.

Equipment

  • 1 Large pot For cooking the meatballs and broth.
  • 1 Mixing bowl For combining the meatball ingredients.

Method
 

Preparation Steps
  1. In a bowl, combine ground beef, minced onion, garlic, fish sauce, salt, pepper, sugar, and cinnamon. Mix gently until just combined. Form the mixture into small meatballs.
  2. In a pot, bring beef broth and star anise to a gentle boil. Carefully add the meatballs to the pot. Simmer for 10–12 minutes until they are cooked through.
  3. While the meatballs are cooking, prepare the rice noodles according to the package instructions. Drain and set aside.
  4. Divide the cooked noodles among bowls. Ladle the hot broth and meatballs over the noodles. Garnish with fresh basil, cilantro, bean sprouts, sliced chili, and lime wedges before serving.

How to Make pho meatballs

This delightful pho meatballs recipe takes about 15 minutes to prepare and 20 minutes to cook. With a little extra time for resting, you’ll have a warm, savory dish ready to enjoy!

Step 1: Prepare the Meatball Mixture

In a bowl, combine ground beef, minced onion, garlic, fish sauce, salt, pepper, sugar, and cinnamon. Mix gently until just combined. Form the mixture into small meatballs.

Step 2: Cook the Meatballs

In a pot, bring beef broth and star anise to a gentle boil. Carefully add the meatballs to the pot. Simmer for 10–12 minutes until they are cooked through.

Step 3: Prepare the Noodles

While the meatballs are cooking, prepare the rice noodles according to the package instructions. Drain and set aside.

Step 4: Assemble and Serve

Divide the cooked noodles among bowls. Ladle the hot broth and meatballs over the noodles. Garnish with fresh basil, cilantro, bean sprouts, sliced chili, and lime wedges before serving.

Recipe Snapshot

Pro Tips for Making pho meatballs

  • Use lean ground beef or chicken for a healthier option.
  • Incorporate fresh herbs like cilantro and green onions for vibrant flavor.
  • Chill the meat mixture before forming meatballs for better texture.
  • Simmer the meatballs gently to keep them tender and juicy.
  • Serve with lime wedges and fresh basil for a refreshing finish.

How to Serve this pho meatballs

  • Serve in a warm bowl of savory broth for a comforting meal.
  • Garnish with fresh herbs like basil, cilantro, and mint for a burst of flavor.
  • Add lime wedges on the side for a zesty kick.
  • Pair with rice noodles for a traditional pho experience.
  • Top with bean sprouts and sliced jalapeños for extra crunch and heat.
  • Enjoy with a side of hoisin sauce and sriracha for dipping.
  • For a lighter option, serve with steamed vegetables instead of noodles.

Make Ahead and Storage

Storing and enjoying your pho meatballs later is easy!

Storing Leftovers

  • Allow meatballs to cool completely.
  • Place in an airtight container.
  • Store in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
  • Keep broth separate to maintain texture.

Freezing

  • Cool meatballs and broth before freezing.
  • Use freezer-safe containers or bags.
  • Label with date and contents.
  • Freeze for up to 3 months for best quality.

Reheating

  • Thaw in the refrigerator overnight if frozen.
  • Reheat broth on the stove until simmering.
  • Add meatballs to the broth to warm through.
  • Microwave meatballs if preferred, but check for even heating.

FAQs

Here’s a helpful FAQ about this recipe:

1. What are the meatballs in pho made of?

Pho meatballs are typically made from a combination of ground beef or chicken, mixed with spices such as garlic, ginger, and green onions. Some recipes also include rice flour or tapioca starch to help bind the meatballs and give them a delightful texture. This combination creates a flavorful and tender meatball that complements the savory broth of pho perfectly.

2. Why are Vietnamese meatballs chewy?

Vietnamese meatballs often have a chewy texture due to the use of certain ingredients like tapioca starch or rice flour, which help create a bouncy consistency. Additionally, the method of mixing the meat thoroughly until it becomes sticky also contributes to this unique texture. This chewiness is a beloved characteristic of authentic Vietnamese meatballs, making them a delightful addition to pho.

3. What are in Vietnamese meatballs?

Vietnamese meatballs typically include ground meat (such as beef or chicken), garlic, shallots, and a blend of spices like black pepper and fish sauce. Some recipes may also incorporate herbs like cilantro or green onions for added flavor. The combination of these ingredients creates a savory and aromatic meatball that enhances the overall taste of pho.

4. What kind of meat goes with pho?

Pho is traditionally made with beef, but you can also use chicken or even seafood for a different twist. Common cuts of beef include brisket, flank, or sirloin, while chicken can be used in the form of shredded meat or whole pieces. The choice of meat can greatly influence the flavor of the broth, so feel free to experiment with your favorites to find the perfect match for your pho!

Final Thoughts

We hope you’re as excited to try these pho meatballs as we are! They’re not just easy to make, but each bite is a warm hug of flavor that brings back memories of cozy family dinners. So gather your ingredients, let the savory broth simmer, and enjoy this delightful dish that’s sure to become a favorite!
